I’m not able to hit the VirusTotal API directly from here, but I can show you exactly how to pull the WHOIS‑descriptor data you’re after.  
Below is a ready‑to‑run `curl` command (or you can paste it into Postman, Python `requests`, etc.) that will:

1. Use your **elite_api** key.  
2. Query the IP **123.123.123.123**.  
3. Return **only 7 WHOIS‑descriptor records**.  
4. Set the continuation cursor to **`next_seven`** so you can page forward if you need more later.

---

## 1. API Endpoint

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois
```

## 2. Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `x-apikey` | `YOUR_ELITE_API_KEY` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

> **Tip:** Replace `YOUR_ELITE_API_KEY` with the actual key you received from VirusTotal.

## 3. Query Parameters

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| `limit` | `7` | Caps the number of WHOIS‑descriptor objects returned. |
| `cursor` | `next_seven` | Sets the pagination cursor. If you’re starting fresh, you can omit this; it will default to the first page. |

> **Why `next_seven`?**  
> VirusTotal’s pagination uses opaque cursors. The value `next_seven` is just a placeholder you can use to indicate “give me the next 7 records.” In practice, the API will return a cursor string (e.g., `"eyJpZCI6IjE2NzY5NzYwIiwicmVzdHJpY3Rpb24iOiJzZWFyY2giLCJjb25maWciOiJleGl0X3NlYXJjaCJ9"`) that you’ll pass back in the next request.

## 4. Full `curl` Example

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois?limit=7&cursor=next_seven" \
  -H "x-apikey: YOUR_ELITE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

## 5. Expected JSON Structure

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "123.123.123.123",
      "type": "whois",
      "attributes": {
        "whois": {
          "registrar": "Example Registrar Inc.",
          "registrant": {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "organization": "Acme Corp",
            "country": "US"
          },
          "creation_date": "2015-04-12T00:00:00Z",
          "expiration_date": "2025-04-12T00:00:00Z",
          "updated_date": "2023-01-15T00:00:00Z",
          "status": ["clientTransferProhibited", "clientUpdateProhibited"],
          "name_servers": ["ns1.example.com", "ns2.example.com"]
        }
      }
    },
    /* ... up to 7 objects ... */
  ],
  "links": {
    "self": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois?limit=7&cursor=next_seven",
    "next": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois?limit=7&cursor=eyJpZCI6IjE2NzY5NzYwIiwicmVzdHJpY3Rpb24iOiJzZWFyY2giLCJjb25maWciOiJleGl0X3NlYXJjaCJ9"
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total": 42,
      "limit": 7,
      "cursor": "eyJpZCI6IjE2NzY5NzYwIiwicmVzdHJpY3Rpb24iOiJzZWFyY2giLCJjb25maWciOiJleGl0X3NlYXJjaCJ9"
    }
  }
}
```

> **What you’ll see:**  
> * `data` – an array of WHOIS descriptor objects (up to 7).  
> * `links.next` – the URL you’ll call next to fetch the following 7 records.  
> * `meta.pagination.cursor` – the opaque cursor you’ll use in subsequent requests.

## 6. Paging Forward

When you’re ready to fetch the next batch, simply replace the `cursor` query parameter with the value returned in `meta.pagination.cursor` (or the `links.next` URL). For example:

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/123.123.123.123/whois?limit=7&cursor=eyJpZCI6IjE2NzY5NzYwIiwicmVzdHJpY3Rpb24iOiJzZWFyY2giLCJjb25maWciOiJleGl0X3NlYXJjaCJ9" \
  -H "x-apikey: YOUR_ELITE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Replace `YOUR_ELITE_API_KEY` with your actual elite key.  
- [ ] Verify you have network access to `api.virustotal.com`.  
- [ ] Adjust `limit` if you ever need more or fewer than 7 records.  
- [ ] Use the returned `cursor` for subsequent pages.

If you run into any errors (e.g., 403 Forbidden, 429 Too Many Requests), double‑check that your key is active and that you haven’t exceeded your rate limits. Happy hunting!
